acceptance_criteria.criterion: The stations CLI command was executed against at least one extracted savegame and the raw JSON output is captured in schema-verification.md.
Each field name in the output is listed with its observed type and a sample value.
The presence or absence of sector, zone, and products fields is explicitly stated.
Any deviation from the plan's assumed field names (componentID, connectionID, name, code, owner, class, macro, state, parentComponent) is flagged with the corrected name.

summary: Executed `bin/query.bat stations --save=125914ba --limit=3 --pretty` against the archived quicksave (ID: 125914ba, 1609 total stations, 15 player-owned).
Captured full raw JSON output in schema-verification.md.
Documented all 9 fields with observed types and sample values.
Confirmed absence of sector, zone, and products fields.
All 9 plan-assumed field names (componentID, connectionID, name, code, owner, class, macro, state, parentComponent) matched exactly — no deviations.
Identified one undocumented optional field: ships (string[]) present on stations with assigned ships — flagged for WP-003.

comments.note: Undiscovered field `ships` (optional string[]) is present on stations with docked/assigned ships. Example: `["ship:[0x7c9bf]"]`. WP-003 must add `ships?: string[]` to the StationData TypeScript interface.
The `class` field is always an empty string in all 1609 observed stations. WP-003 UI implementation should treat it as always-empty and avoid displaying it unless a non-empty value is detected.
The `name` field is empty for NPC stations. WP-003 UI should fall back to displaying `code` when `name` is empty to ensure all rows have a meaningful identifier.

summary: WP-002 is a pure research/documentation deliverable — no implementation code to review. Evaluated schema-verification.md against all four acceptance criteria and overall document quality.
AC1 PASS: Two raw JSON samples captured (NPC sample + player-owned sample), providing good data variety that directly reveals the optional `ships` field.
AC2 PASS: Field inventory table is complete — all 10 observed fields listed with type, always-present flag, and dual sample values (NPC and player column).
AC3 PASS: `sector`, `zone`, and `products` confirmed ABSENT with clear rationale (location encoded only in `parentComponent`).
AC4 PASS: All 9 assumed field names match exactly in name and camelCase — no deviations. Zero corrections required.
Bonus discovery: `ships?: string[]` optional field correctly identified and documented with format notes. Recommendation to add to WP-003 StationData interface is precise and actionable.
Document structure is logical: header metadata → raw samples → field inventory → absence confirmation → deviation comparison → unexpected fields → WP-003 recommendations. No improvements needed.

comments.note: The two-sample approach (NPC + player-owned) was excellent methodology — it directly surfaced the optional `ships` field that a single generic sample would likely have missed. This pattern (show data for both the common case and the edge case) is worth reusing in future schema verification WPs.

The `parentComponent` format `"zone:[hex]"` encodes the zone ID. WP-003 may wish to document whether this value is useful for display or filtering; currently the plan excludes sector/zone filtering, so no action needed — recorded for awareness only.
